definitions.meaning: A comparison of parts of one whole: 2:3 means 2 parts for one share and 3 parts for the other, with every part the same size.
One equal piece of the split whole: when $48 is shared in 2:3 there are 5 parts, and one part is $9.60.
The full amount being shared: in sharing $48 in the ratio 2:3 the whole is $48, split into 5 equal parts.
The amount one person gets: the number of parts they take multiplied by one part, such as 3 x $9.60 = $28.80.

mechanismSteps: Sharing in a ratio: two children share $48 in the ratio 2:3 - split the money into 2 parts for child A and 3 parts for child B, 5 equal parts in all.
Watch out: 3:2 is not 3/2 of the whole: the parts are counted out of the 5 parts of the whole, so 3 parts is 3/5 of the whole, never 3/2 of it.
One part, then multiply: 5 equal parts share $48, so 1 part = $9.60 - then multiply: A gets 2 x $9.60 = $19.20 and B gets 3 x $9.60 = $28.80.
The takeaway: to share in a ratio, add the parts to find the whole in parts, divide to find one part, then multiply for each share.
objectives: Read a ratio as equal parts of one whole: 2:3 as 2 parts and 3 parts of the same whole
Share an amount in a ratio by finding one part first: divide the whole by the total number of parts
subject: math
title: Ratio: sharing $48 in 2:3

trap.explanation: The ratio parts are mistaken for a fraction of the whole. The whole is 5 parts, so 3 parts is 3 fifths of the whole. In the animation scene s2 the claim is tested against the whole bar and fails: 3/2 of $48 is $72, more than the whole $48, while 3 parts out of 5 is $28.80.
trap.misconception: A ratio of 3:2 means 3/2 of the whole.

workedExample: In scene s3, sharing $48 in the ratio 2:3 is worked by finding one part first: the whole is 2 + 3 = 5 parts, and 1 part = $9.60 (from $48 / 5). Step by step: A gets 2 x $9.60 = $19.20 and B gets 3 x $9.60 = $28.80, and the shares check: $19.20 + $28.80 = $48.
